q1: SELECT b.name AS bar, COUNT(DISTINCT f.drinker) AS num_drinker, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price, (SELECT f1.drinker FROM frequents AS f1 WHERE f1.bar = b.name ORDER BY f1.times_a_week DESC, f1.drinker ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_reg_drinker FROM bar AS b LEFT JOIN frequents AS f ON b.name = f.bar LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.bar GROUP BY b.name ORDER BY num_drinker DESC, b.name ASC
q2: SELECT b.name, COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT f.drinker), 0) AS total_num_drinker, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price, (SELECT d.drinker FROM Frequents AS d WHERE d.bar = b.name GROUP BY d.drinker ORDER BY COUNT(d.times_a_week) DESC, d.drinker ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_reg_drinker FROM Bar AS b LEFT JOIN Frequents AS f ON b.name = f.bar LEFT JOIN Serves AS s ON b.name = s.bar GROUP BY b.name ORDER BY total_num_drinker DESC, b.name ASC

explanation: Q1 and Q2 differ in how they handle the calculation of the 'most_reg_drinker' subquery. Q1 orders by 'times_a_week' in descending order and 'drinker' in ascending order, while Q2 orders by 'times_a_week' in descending order and groups by 'drinker' without an order by clause. This can lead to different results if there are ties in 'times_a_week' or if the 'drinker' column has non-unique values.
